title: The pure in heart (Matthew 5:8)
hookLine: the pure in heart shall see God

cards: Count the tabs open on your screen right now. Or in your head. A lot of life happens in split screen: listening to a friend while checking a phone, eating while scrolling, praying while making the grocery list.
It's rare to be all in one place. The sixth line of the sermon makes a startling promise: some people will see God. And it says who: not the smartest, not the most religious.

teach.b: In the King James Bible: "Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God." Pure sounds like spotless, never done anything wrong. But the Greek word, katharos, is more like clean, clear, unmixed.
Greek writers could use it of clean water, of metal with no alloy, of grain with the chaff winnowed out. And heart, in the Bible, isn't just feelings.

teach.h: THE HEART: THE CENTER OF A PERSON.
teach.b: It's the center of a person: where you think, choose and want. So a pure heart is an unmixed one. A single heart, not divided between God and ten other things, not saying one thing and wanting another.
A psalm asked long ago: "Who shall ascend into the hill of the LORD? or who shall stand in his holy place? He that hath clean hands, and a pure heart."
In the nineteenth century, the Danish writer Soren Kierkegaard called a book Purity of Heart Is to Will One Thing. That's close. And the promise: they shall see God.
Christians understand that in more than one way. Some look first to a final vision of God, face to face.
Others also say the pure in heart start seeing God now, in a face, in bread, in a quiet morning, because they're finally looking in one direction.

Look back at this first week on the mountain. Jesus sat down, then blessed the empty-handed, the mourners, the meek, the hungry for good, the merciful, and now the single-hearted. Each one is a way of being open.

how: Some Christians pray for a clean heart in the words of Psalm 51, and practices like examining the conscience, confession and silent prayer are meant to gather a scattered heart back to one center.

o: spotless, with no wrong ever done in your whole life
clean and unmixed, like water or metal with nothing added
bright and shining, glowing with a heavenly light

p: clean hands, and a pure heart
purity of heart is to will one thing

s: pure in heart means never having done anything wrong
katharos means unmixed: a single heart, not a spotless record.
a psalm already joins clean hands and a pure heart
Psalm 24: he that hath clean hands, and a pure heart.
in the Bible, heart means only emotions

games.q: you're listening to a friend while half-reading a message. the beatitude says the pure in heart see God. what's katharos asking of you?
o: be unmixed: all in one place.
games.why: katharos means clean, unmixed. a single heart, looking in one direction, is the one that sees.

practice: For these two minutes, do only one thing: breathe. When your mind opens another tab, and it will, notice it, close it gently, and come back to the breath; wandering isn't failing, the practice is the coming back.
If you pray, you can offer this one undivided moment to God.

wordCard.voice: Katharos, the Greek word for clean, clear, unmixed. A single heart, not split ten ways, and the promise that it shall see God.

orig.note: Greek: the pure, the clean. Matthew 5:8. the singular is katharos.

carryVoice: Your line: a single heart sees. Pure means unmixed, not spotless. That's one week on the mountain, done.
